mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. Have you ever noticed how the thought of our own mortality, even if we rarely speak of it, quietly shapes so much of what we do? It's something most of us push aside, but deep down, it colors our ambitions, our dreams, and even the stories we tell ourselves about who we are. Together, we're about to explore these hidden currents through the lens of The Denial of Death by Ernest Becker. Becker invites us to look right at the heart of a paradox: we’re driven to find meaning and significance, all while knowing that our time here isn’t forever. That tension? It’s more powerful than we might think. It sparks creativity, fuels our drive, and sometimes makes us cling to beliefs and myths that help protect us from the fear of the unknown. As we peel back the layers of denial and defense, we’ll see how the dance between fear and creativity shapes our lives. Why do we chase after purpose? Why do we crave validation or dream of something lasting, even when we know everything changes? Becker’s insights reveal that facing our own mortality doesn’t just bring anxiety—it can also set us free, inspiring us to live more authentically and bravely. So, as we journey together through these ideas, let’s stay curious. What if understanding our relationship with death could actually help us embrace life more fully—with a little more courage and a lot more clarity? Let’s dive in and discover what really drives us as human beings—side by side, one step at a time.
